stories.what: Life Biosciences reported interim data from three people with glaucoma given a single eye injection of its cell-resetting gene therapy ER-100 plus daily doxycycline. It was well tolerated through day 56, the safety board recommended a higher dose, and two of three people showed possible visual-field improvement.
stories.why: First human data on partial reprogramming; open-label, three people, safety-focused. The records already hold a 2026-10-08 announcement of the same data, so this 10-27 post may be a repost, not new data.

stories.what: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 410 people with early Parkinson's disease found that a year of twice-daily nicotinamide riboside (a precursor that raises cell NAD) did not improve symptoms. Nature Aging ran a news summary of the result.
stories.why: Largest controlled test of an NAD-raising supplement for a clinical outcome and it was negative; bears directly on the NAD record, though the disease is Parkinson's, not ageing as such. Only the news summary was readable (the paper is paywalled).

stories.what: A Nature Aging paper reports that vanadyl sulfate, a mineral supplement, acts as a senolytic (it kills aged cells), and that taken by mouth it reduced ageing features and extended lifespan in male mice.
stories.why: Another mouse lifespan result for clearing aged cells, with a cheap oral compound; male mice only and no human data.

stories.what: A senolytic vaccine that trains T cells to attack aged cells raised median lifespan 12 percent in female mice when given late in life, with lower aged-cell markers. The reviewer notes the control mice were short-lived, which weakens the result.
stories.source_kind: lifespan.io news (reporting an Advanced Science paper)
stories.why: Immune route to clearing aged cells with a lifespan effect; caveat about short-lived controls limits it.

stories.what: Overexpressing SRSF1, an RNA-processing factor, in mouse liver rejuvenated human cells in culture and extended lifespan and reduced frailty in mice, as an alternative to Yamanaka-factor reprogramming.
stories.why: A new rejuvenation route that avoids the cell-identity loss of reprogramming; animal and cell data only.

stories.what: A report covered by Fight Aging! describes circular RNA carrying the Yamanaka factors that produced partial reprogramming without pushing cells to full pluripotency.
stories.why: Delivery-method advance for partial reprogramming; cell-level, I did not identify the underlying paper's venue.

stories.what: Nature reported on a growing push to extend pet lifespans after the first Animal Longevity Summit in Toronto, including gene therapies for dogs and the commercial race around them.
stories.why: Mainstream coverage of the dog-longevity field that the dog-approval record and Loyal's 2025 approval-by-end-of-2025 claim depend on; I did not find in it a new approval, and did not read it in full.

stories.what: In a placebo-controlled trial published in a cardiology journal, the multi-ingredient supplement NOVOS Core improved artery function and systolic blood pressure in people around 60. The company funded the study and the effect cannot be traced to any ingredient.
stories.source_kind: lifespan.io news (reporting European Heart Journal Open paper)
stories.why: A controlled human trial of a longevity supplement, but industry-funded, one blend, and a vascular measure rather than ageing.

stories.what: Lifespan Research Institute's editorial says regulators and investors are shifting toward aging biology, pointing to FDA leaders naming longevity a priority at a conference and to new funding.
stories.why: Opinion piece by an advocacy group. The underlying FDA panel story is dated 2026-10-02, before the window, and the officials discussed endpoints and pathways, not declaring ageing a disease.

stories.what: The FDA issued final guidance on how makers of cell and gene therapies must assure each batch's potency, replacing its 2011 guidance.
stories.why: General regulatory clarity for gene and cell therapies, which rejuvenation approaches would rely on; not specific to ageing.

stories.what: The FDA opened an investigation of Novartis's gene therapy Zolgensma after cancer cases were reported.
stories.source_kind: trade press headline (Endpoints News, article blocked)
stories.why: A gene-therapy safety signal relevant to any in-body gene therapy for ageing. Only the RSS headline and date were read; detail unverified.

stories.what: Endpoints reported at the American Heart Association meeting that heart drugs from Novo Nordisk and Novartis failed in similar, surprising ways.
stories.source_kind: trade press headline (Endpoints News, article blocked)
stories.why: Possibly the full presentation of Novo's ziltivekimab ZEUS result, which the records already hold from 2026-07-31; I could not open the article to confirm which drugs.

stories.what: Endpoints reported at the American Heart Association meeting that Amgen's Repatha cuts heart-attack risk.
stories.source_kind: trade press headline (Endpoints News, article blocked)
stories.why: Cardiovascular prevention news, not ageing-specific; headline only.

stories.what: A genetics-and-biomarker item identifies blood plasma proteins linked to mortality risk and biological age.
stories.why: Headline and date only from the feed; I did not open the page.

stories.what: A Cell paper reports that fatty acid desaturation decides whether a stressed cell becomes senescent or dies by ferroptosis.
stories.why: Basic biology of aged cells; the page was not opened, only the Europe PMC listing entry.

stories.what: A trial of fisetin for vascular function in older adults is registered (phase 2, University of Colorado Boulder, not yet recruiting, start 2026-11).
stories.why: A new controlled test of a senolytic candidate; registry entry only, no results.
